setup_data_boundary: Use your own original PC Duke Nukem 3D data folder, anchored by DUKE3D.GRP. Raze recognizes retail 1.3/Atomic and specific World Tour data variants; the actual group-file identity selects the edition. Keep the accompanying original files. Console, mobile and other Raze games are not substitutes. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze, or add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

On Windows, use the official Windows ZIP and select raze.exe with the extracted player folder as its working directory. Keep the DLLs, raze.pk3 and soundfonts together. Registration does not start the player; Play does. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your DUKE3D.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

You and upstream replace this external player. Portcove registration preserves every external file and does not promise managed Update, Backup or Rollback. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. Linux has no native archive in this selected GitHub release: use an already prepared upstream/system-package copy or upstream’s build instructions, then its native player. Linux normally uses ~/.config/raze for configuration and savegames, and can move an older ~/.raze directory on first use. Platform handoffs do not establish native execution or save compatibility.
